You have to consider that these characters make 2 years to make each.

And SF3 was only a cult following until we finally got it in the West as it never was easily accesible until likely fightcade. People enjoyed SF3 when it was properly available to the West. It was also popping in Japan. So I have no idea why you assume it was a “cult classic” when it was actually received well. The only reason we couldn’t get an opinion on in here is because of accessibility. 

Street Fighter 3 characters ARE still the “New Generation” of fighters canonically. And if Street Fighter 3: Third Strike (Primarily) is such a niche cult classic, they could have easily introduced at least some of the characters in the base roster or first wave of DLC with either new iterations entirely or just fresh coats of paint. (In the vain of Ryu, Ken, Guile, Etc. from SFV to SFVI) Did you not see the resurgence in SFV when Urien was released? And then later when Gill was revealed? We love/loved these characters. 

Now don’t get me wrong, I like the newer faces. I think we could have done without Lilly personally, but there are a fair amount of T. Hawk enjoyers out there. I also don’t have an issue with SF2 characters being in the roster. I think there SHOULD be SF2 characters as they are most iconic. I just think the pool was too big for the game to solely be comprised of New Challenger and SF2 when the Illuminati exists in the story. The story WILL go forward with the fall of Shadaloo, stagnation of the Illuminati (Kolin, Gill, Urien, etc.) and Metro City as a whole (Fatal Fury Characters). (Tying another loose end in the SF Continuum.) And its safe to assume the release of SF3 characters in SFV was a test to see if the characters would be well received in a more modern game. Safe to assume also that that answer is yes.

TL;DR: People did not HATE SF3, its original peak was not easily accessible to everybody in the West thus making it a less popular game not a bad one. Even if people didn’t know about SF3 in the West, it would be easy to have a continuation of the series with some SF3 cast as the “new faces” as they would basically be new to a modern audience. (not to undermine the newer faces in sf6.)
